answer: Distinct-substrate binding: each identity must anchor to a unique physical host with a measured hardware fingerprint plus a continuous power-draw trace signed by a co-located meter. Enrollment requires the host to harbor a fixed latency signature from a local probe, which clones on identical hardware cannot replicate without separate bodies. Attackers must rent distinct machines, each traced through a dune of varying thermal noise, costing thousands per identity. A glacier of accumulated meter records makes retroactive duplication detectable.
